To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the deletion of the first three 17-bp repeat elements in the oriV region of RK2 leads to a loss of plasmid replication in E. coli but does not affect plasmid replication and copy number in A tumefaciens.
two deletions of the broad-host range plasmid RK 2, which lost the first two (smaller deletion) and the first three (larger deletion) of the 17-bp repeated sequences of oriV, were isolated.
two spontaneous deletions in the RK2 origin of replication (oril) have been identified and characterized.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms of plasmid replication.
the molecular basis of the broad host-range of the plasmid RK6.
the replication of plasmids and their role in the transfer of genes between bacteria.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the oriV sequences are important for the initiation of plasmid replication in A. tumecfascens and that they are also important for the initiation and the termination of plasmid replicaiton in E. coli.
the oriV sequences of pRK2 have a role in copy number control of the plasmid in A. tumifaciens and are essential for replication in E. coli. Replication of the Broad-Host-Range
the 17-bp repeat sequences of the RK2 ori region play a role in the replication of the plasmid in both hosts.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the oriV sequences play an important role in the regulation of plasmid copy numbers in E. coli and A. tumefacians, and that these sequences are essential for the replication of pK2 in E. coli but are not for its replication in A. tumifaciens.
the RK2 plasmid has a complex replication system.
the 17-bp direct repeats are important in the replication of RK2 and that the 3' end of the 17-bps repeats are important in replication of RK2 in E. coli.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the 17-bp repeat sequences in RK2 oriV are important in copy number control in A. tumecfasciens and that the loss of the first three repeats in the larger deletion leads to a complete loss of plasmid replication in E. coli.
the deletion of a few nucleotides in the origin of replication region of RK2 leads to a loss of replication in E. coli, but not in Agrobacteriurn.
the deletion of 56 bp near the origin of plasmid RK-2 can lead to a significant increase in plasmid replication in A. tumifaciens.
